title: Human Cell Anatomy & Organelles
subject: Biology
alt: Labelled diagram of a human cell showing internal organelles
description: Cross-sectional anatomy of a human animal cell showing the plasma membrane, nucleus, mitochondria, rough ER, and Golgi apparatus.

regions.label: Cell Membrane
regions.note: The flexible lipid bilayer enclosing the human cell and regulating what enters and leaves.

regions.label: Nucleus (DNA)
regions.note: The master control center storing genomic chromosomal DNA and coordinating gene expression.

regions.label: Mitochondria (ATP Powerhouse)
regions.note: The powerhouse organelle executing cellular respiration to generate ATP energy.

regions.label: Rough ER & Ribosomes
regions.note: Folded membranous highway studded with ribosomes that synthesize and fold secretory proteins.

regions.label: Golgi Apparatus
regions.note: Flattened membranous sacs that sort, modify, and package proteins into vesicles.

regions.label: Cytoplasm (Cytosol)
regions.note: The water-rich nutrient jelly filling the cellular interior and suspending organelles.

title: Annotated Human Cell
subject: Biology
alt: Labelled diagram of a human cell showing organelles
description: Cross-section of a human animal cell showing the plasma membrane, nucleus, mitochondria, rough ER, and Golgi apparatus.

regions.label: Cell membrane
regions.note: The cell membrane is the outer lipid bilayer controlling what enters and leaves the cell.

regions.label: Nucleus (DNA)
regions.note: The nucleus stores chromosomal DNA and controls gene expression and cellular activity.

regions.label: Mitochondria
regions.note: Mitochondria generate ATP chemical energy via aerobic cellular respiration.

regions.label: Rough ER
regions.note: The rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with ribosomes that synthesize and fold proteins.

regions.label: Golgi body
regions.note: The Golgi body sorts, packages, and tags proteins into vesicles for distribution.

title: Annotated Water Cycle
subject: Earth Science
alt: Labelled diagram of the hydrologic water cycle
description: Continuous movement of water on, above, and below the surface of the Earth driven by solar radiation and gravity.

regions.label: Sun (Solar Energy)
regions.note: The Sun provides thermal radiation that warms water bodies and powers evaporation.

regions.label: Evaporation
regions.note: Liquid water absorbs latent heat and transforms into invisible gaseous water vapour.

regions.label: Condensation (Clouds)
regions.note: Water vapour rises, expands, and cools, condensing onto nuclei into visible clouds.

regions.label: Precipitation
regions.note: Water droplets grow heavy enough for gravitational pull to cause rain or snow.

regions.label: Collection (Runoff & Lake)
regions.note: Precipitation flows into lakes, streams, and aquifers, ready to restart the cycle.

title: DC Electric Circuit
subject: Physics
alt: Labelled DC electric circuit diagram with battery, switch, resistor, and lamp
description: Complete electrical loop with DC voltage source, control switch, series resistor, and resistive lamp load showing current direction.

regions.label: Battery (DC Source)
regions.note: The battery provides electromotive force (EMF) creating a potential difference across the circuit.

regions.label: Control Switch
regions.note: The switch controls circuit continuity; when closed, conductive contact allows electrons to flow.

regions.label: Resistor (R)
regions.note: The resistor impedes electric current according to Ohm's Law (V = IR) and dissipates heat.

regions.label: Lamp / Load
regions.note: The lamp converts electrical energy into luminous radiation and thermal heat.

regions.label: Current Flow (I)
regions.note: Conventional electric current flows from the positive terminal toward the negative terminal.

title: Inclined Plane Mechanics
subject: Physics
alt: Labelled physics free body diagram on an inclined plane
description: Classical Newtonian mechanics problem showing resolving forces: normal force FN, gravitational weight Fg = mg, friction fk, and pulling force Fpull on a wedge at angle theta.

regions.label: Mass Block (m)
regions.note: The block of mass m rests on the inclined slope with angle θ.

regions.label: Normal Force (F_N)
regions.note: Normal force acts perpendicular to the inclined surface with magnitude F_N = mg cos θ.

regions.label: Kinetic Friction (f_k)
regions.note: Kinetic friction opposes sliding motion parallel to the plane: f_k = μ · F_N.

regions.label: Gravity Force (F_g = mg)
regions.note: Gravity pulls vertically downward toward Earth's centre with magnitude F_g = mg.

regions.label: Pulling Force (F_pull)
regions.note: Applied force pulling the block up the incline against component of gravity and friction.

regions.label: Incline Angle (θ)
regions.note: The angle θ dictates the splitting of gravitational force into parallel and perpendicular components.

title: Human Heart & Blood Flow
subject: Anatomy & Biology
alt: Labelled diagram of the human heart showing internal chambers, valves, and circulatory blood flow
description: Cross-sectional anatomy of the human heart showing four chambers (atria, ventricles), heart valves (tricuspid, bicuspid, pulmonary, aortic), and major vessels (aorta, vena cava, pulmonary vessels).
prompts: “Trace deoxygenated blood through the right atrium”

regions.label: Superior Vena Cava
regions.note: Large vein delivering deoxygenated systemic blood from the head, neck, arms, and upper chest directly into the right atrium.

regions.label: Inferior Vena Cava
regions.note: Large vein returning deoxygenated venous blood from lower limbs and abdomen into the right atrium.

regions.label: Right Atrium
regions.note: Receives deoxygenated blood from the superior and inferior vena cava and pumps it through the tricuspid valve into the right ventricle.

regions.label: Tricuspid Valve
regions.note: Three-cusp valve preventing retrograde backflow of blood from right ventricle into right atrium during ventricular systole.

regions.label: Right Ventricle
regions.note: Muscular lower chamber pumping deoxygenated blood through the pulmonary valve into the pulmonary trunk toward the lungs.

regions.label: Pulmonary Valve
regions.note: Semilunar valve preventing backflow of blood from pulmonary artery back into right ventricle during diastole.

regions.label: Pulmonary Artery
regions.note: Carries deoxygenated blood from right ventricle branching into left and right pulmonary arteries toward both lungs for gas exchange.

regions.label: Aorta (Systemic Arch)
regions.note: Primary and largest systemic artery distributing high-pressure oxygenated blood from left ventricle to the entire body.

regions.label: Pulmonary Veins
regions.note: Four veins transporting newly oxygenated blood from the lungs directly into the left atrium.

regions.label: Left Atrium
regions.note: Receives oxygen-rich blood returning from the pulmonary veins and funnels it through the bicuspid valve into the left ventricle.

regions.label: Bicuspid (Mitral) Valve
regions.note: Dual-flap valve preventing backflow from the high-pressure left ventricle into left atrium during contraction.

regions.label: Aortic Valve
regions.note: Semilunar valve between left ventricle and aorta preventing backflow into ventricle when relaxing.

regions.label: Left Ventricle
regions.note: Thickest, most muscular chamber generating systemic arterial pressure to propel oxygenated blood throughout the human body.

regions.label: Interventricular Septum
regions.note: Thick muscular partition separating the left and right ventricles, preventing mixing of oxygen-rich and oxygen-poor blood.

title: Mitochondria Anatomy & ATP Synthesis
subject: Biology
alt: Labelled diagram of a mitochondrion showing outer membrane, inner membrane, cristae, matrix, DNA, ribosomes, and ATP synthase
description: Cross-sectional anatomy of a mitochondrion illustrating the double membrane architecture, folded cristae, matrix fluid, circular mtDNA, ribosomes, and F0F1-ATPase synthase.

regions.label: Outer Membrane
regions.note: Smooth, continuous phospholipid bilayer containing porin protein channels allowing nutrient passage.

regions.label: Inner Membrane
regions.note: Selectively permeable inner lipid bilayer housing electron transport chain complexes.

regions.label: Cristae (Inner Folds)
regions.note: Deep convoluted inward folds of the inner membrane maximizing surface area for ATP synthase machinery.

regions.label: Mitochondrial Matrix
regions.note: Enzyme-dense inner fluid hosting the Krebs citric acid cycle, circular mtDNA, and ribosomes.

regions.label: Intermembrane Space
regions.note: Narrow fluid compartment where protons (H+) accumulate to establish the chemiosmotic gradient.

regions.label: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA)
regions.note: Maternally inherited circular genome encoding essential respiratory chain proteins.

regions.label: Mitochondrial Ribosomes
regions.note: Specialized 70S ribosomes synthesizing hydrophobic subunits of respiratory complexes.

regions.label: F0F1-ATPase (ATP Synthase)
regions.note: Rotary nanomachine driven by proton motive force to synthesize ATP from ADP and phosphate.
